_about: Curated source list for LAMPLIGHT. Hand-edited. scripts/build-catalogue.mjs resolves each entry against archive.org (MP3 URL, duration, reader) and writes data/catalogue.json. 'match' is a case-insensitive regex tested against the archive.org file title; several matching files play in order as one story.

entries.title: The Darling
entries.author: Anton Chekhov
entries.hook: Olenka loves whoever is nearest, and adopts his opinions on timber, theatre and veterinary science.

entries.title: The Bet
entries.author: Anton Chekhov
entries.hook: Fifteen years of voluntary solitude, two million roubles, and a banker who would rather not pay.

entries.title: Three Questions
entries.author: Leo Tolstoy
entries.hook: A king wants three answers and gets them from a hermit who is busy digging.

entries.title: The Tryst
entries.author: Ivan Turgenev
entries.hook: A birch wood in autumn, a hunter hidden in it, and a valet who is leaving for good.

entries.title: Moonlight
entries.author: Guy de Maupassant
entries.hook: A priest who distrusts women goes out with a stick to catch his niece, and is undone by the night.

entries.title: My Uncle Jules
entries.author: Guy de Maupassant
entries.hook: A family waits on the Le Havre jetty every Sunday for a rich relative, then meets him selling oysters.

entries.title: The Umbrella
entries.author: Guy de Maupassant
entries.hook: Madame Oreille cannot bear to spend money, so she makes an insurance company pay for an umbrella.

entries.title: The Three Low Masses
entries.author: Alphonse Daudet
entries.hook: A chaplain gallops through three Christmas masses because the turkeys are already roasting.

entries.title: The Louis d'Or
entries.author: François Coppée
entries.hook: A ruined young man in Paris, a gold coin, and Christmas Eve.

entries.title: A Christmas in the Forest
entries.author: André Theuriet
entries.hook: A short Christmas piece from the forest country of Lorraine. Nine minutes.

entries.title: The Poet's Christmas Eve
entries.author: Pedro Antonio de Alarcón
entries.hook: Alarcón, away from Andalusia, remembers Christmas Eve at home.

entries.title: Maese Pérez the Organist
entries.author: Gustavo Adolfo Bécquer
entries.hook: Seville's best organist dies, and the organ at midnight mass goes on playing anyway.

entries.title: Captain Veneno's Proposal of Marriage
entries.author: Pedro Antonio de Alarcón
entries.hook: A famously bad-tempered captain proposes in the most insulting way he can manage.

entries.match: Legend Of The Rose Of The Alhambra
entries.title: Legend of the Rose of the Alhambra
entries.author: Washington Irving
entries.hook: A page chasing a falcon finds a girl in a locked tower, and an old lute that will only play for her.

entries.title: The Ugly Duckling
entries.author: Hans Christian Andersen
entries.hook: You know how it ends. Andersen takes his time getting there, and the duck yard is funnier than you remember.

entries.title: The Swineherd
entries.author: Hans Christian Andersen
entries.hook: A prince in disguise sells a princess a musical saucepan for a hundred kisses.

entries.title: Lasse, My Thrall!
entries.author: Swedish folk tale (ed. Clara Stroebe)
entries.hook: A poor boy inherits an invisible servant who does anything asked of him and would quite like a day off.

entries.title: Thor's Wonderful Journey
entries.author: Mary H. Foster & Mabel H. Cummings (retelling)
entries.hook: Thor loses a drinking contest, a race and a wrestling match, all to things that are not quite what they look like.

entries.title: Holland (from Hans Brinker)
entries.author: Mary Mapes Dodge
entries.hook: An American's tour of a country held together by dykes, windmills and very careful housekeeping.

entries.title: Araby
entries.author: James Joyce
entries.hook: A boy promises to bring a girl something from the bazaar, and his uncle comes home late.

entries.title: Clay
entries.author: James Joyce
entries.hook: Maria crosses Dublin on Halloween with plumcake, and nobody tells her she sang the wrong verse.

entries.title: The Selfish Giant
entries.author: Oscar Wilde
entries.hook: A giant walls off his garden from children, and spring declines to come in either.

entries.match: Its Walls Were as of Jasper
entries.title: Its Walls Were as of Jasper
entries.author: Kenneth Grahame
entries.hook: A small boy on a dull visit finds an illuminated book and walks into the walled city in its pictures.

entries.title: Habetrot the Spinstress
entries.author: Scottish folk tale (ed. Elizabeth W. Grierson)
entries.hook: A lazy girl, seven heads of lint, and a fairy spinster whose lips are worn flat from the thread.

entries.match: The Seal Catcher and the Merman
entries.title: The Seal Catcher and the Merman
entries.author: Scottish folk tale (ed. Elizabeth W. Grierson)
entries.hook: A seal hunter on the far north coast is taken under the sea to meet the seal he wounded.

entries.title: The Bridges of Florence
entries.author: Anna Cora Mowatt
entries.hook: An American actress walks the bridges of Florence in the 1850s and tells their histories.

entries.title: The Shipwrecked Sailor
entries.author: Ancient Egyptian tale (tr. W. M. Flinders Petrie)
entries.hook: Four thousand years old: a sailor washed up on an island ruled by a kindly, very large golden serpent.

entries.title: Rasselas, Chapters I–IV: The Happy Valley
entries.author: Samuel Johnson
entries.hook: A prince lives in a valley where every wish is met, and finds that this is the problem.

entries.title: The Lost Joy
entries.author: Olive Schreiner
entries.hook: Ten minutes of allegory about Love, Joy and what comes after them, written on a Karoo farm.

entries.title: How Jakhals Fed Oom Leeuw
entries.author: Sanni Metelerkamp
entries.hook: Jackal and Uncle Lion, as told by Outa Karel on a Karoo farm.

entries.title: The Elephant's Child
entries.author: Rudyard Kipling
entries.hook: An elephant with satiable curtiosity goes to the great grey-green, greasy Limpopo River to ask what the Crocodile has for dinner.

entries.title: The Coming of the Ship
entries.author: Kahlil Gibran
entries.hook: The opening of The Prophet: twelve years waiting, then a ship in the harbour and a town that does not want him to go.

entries.title: The Cabuliwallah
entries.author: Rabindranath Tagore
entries.hook: A five-year-old in Calcutta befriends an Afghan fruit-seller with a bag of raisins and a daughter at home.

entries.match: How the Camel got his Hump
entries.title: How the Camel Got His Hump
entries.author: Rudyard Kipling
entries.hook: The Camel says 'Humph' once too often, and a Djinn has had enough.

entries.title: In Bangkok
entries.author: Frank G. Carpenter
entries.hook: A 1920s American travel writer's first impressions of Bangkok. Period attitudes included.

entries.title: The Golden Pagoda
entries.author: Frank G. Carpenter
entries.hook: The Shwedagon in Rangoon, described by a 1920s American visitor.

entries.title: Baguio
entries.author: Frank G. Carpenter
entries.hook: The pine-covered hill station above Manila, seen by a 1920s American visitor, with the attitudes of his time.

entries.title: Celebration of the New Year
entries.author: Herbert A. Giles
entries.hook: A British consul's short 1870s notes on how China saw in the New Year.

entries.title: The Sky Bridge of Birds
entries.author: Korean folk tale (ed. William Elliot Griffis)
entries.hook: A herdsman and a weaver in the sky, kept apart by a river of stars, meet once a year on a bridge of magpies.

entries.match: The Woodman and the Mountain Fairies
entries.title: The Woodman and the Mountain Fairies
entries.author: Korean folk tale (ed. William Elliot Griffis)
entries.hook: A woodcutter wanders into the mountains and meets the fairies who live there.

entries.title: Bon-Odori
entries.author: Lafcadio Hearn
entries.hook: Hearn rides into a village in summer and watches the dance for the returning dead go on by lantern light until very late.

entries.title: The Pier
entries.author: Mori Ōgai
entries.hook: A young wife on the Yokohama pier, seeing her husband off.

entries.title: Ukiyoe
entries.author: Nagai Kafū
entries.hook: Kafū on old woodblock prints of Edo and the city they recorded.

entries.title: The Wonderful Tea-Kettle
entries.author: Japanese folk tale (ed. William Elliot Griffis)
entries.hook: A priest's kettle grows a badger's tail when it is put on the fire, and turns out to have a stage career in it.

entries.title: The Voyage
entries.author: Katherine Mansfield
entries.hook: A girl and her grandmother take the night ferry from Wellington to Picton. Swan umbrella, cabin, and a cup of tea.

entries.title: Her First Ball
entries.author: Katherine Mansfield
entries.hook: Leila's first dance card, and one fat old partner who tells her exactly how this will end.

entries.title: Hills of Faery: The Little People of the Mist
entries.author: James Cowan
entries.hook: The patupaiarehe, the fairy people said to live in the mist on the Port Hills above Christchurch.

entries.title: The Bush Undertaker
entries.author: Henry Lawson
entries.hook: An old shepherd alone with his dog on Christmas Day finds an old mate and gives him a ceremony. Dry, odd and a little macabre: vet this one.

entries.title: Letter #5: Board and Lodging Secured
entries.author: Mark Twain
entries.hook: Twain, 1866, settles into lodgings in Honolulu and files his report to a Sacramento paper.

entries.title: The Jumping Frog
entries.author: Mark Twain
entries.hook: The frog story, then a French translation of it, then Twain translating the French back into English.

entries.title: The Ransom of Red Chief
entries.author: O. Henry
entries.hook: Two kidnappers take a ten-year-old and then try to pay his father to take him back.

entries.title: The Gift of the Magi
entries.author: O. Henry
entries.hook: One dollar and eighty-seven cents in an eight-dollar flat, the day before Christmas.

entries.title: Green Island
entries.author: Sarah Orne Jewett
entries.hook: Mrs Todd rows the narrator out to the island where her mother lives.

entries.title: The Whirlwind Campaign in Mariposa
entries.author: Stephen Leacock
entries.hook: Mariposa tries to raise money for the church in one week of organised enthusiasm.

entries.title: L'Envoi: The Train to Mariposa
entries.author: Stephen Leacock
entries.hook: Rich men in a city club, and the evening train that would take them back to the small town they came from.

entries.title: Hurrying Ludovic
entries.author: L. M. Montgomery
entries.hook: Ludovic Speed has been courting Theodora Dix for years. Anne decides it is time he got on with it.

entries.title: The Floating Gardens
entries.author: Nellie Bly
entries.hook: Nellie Bly, 1886, out on the canals at the edge of Mexico City.

entries.match: My First Visit to Buenos Ayres
entries.title: My First Visit to Buenos Ayres
entries.author: W. H. Hudson
entries.hook: A boy from the pampas sees Buenos Aires for the first time.

entries.title: Aspects of the Plain
entries.author: W. H. Hudson
entries.hook: The flat grass country of Hudson's childhood, and the sky above it.

entries.title: Life!
entries.author: Machado de Assis
entries.hook: At the end of time the Wandering Jew talks with Prometheus about whether he would do it all again.

entries.title: Babylon
entries.author: Louisa Jebb
entries.hook: Two Englishwomen reach the ruins of Babylon in 1908.

foreign.title: Les Étoiles
foreign.author: Alphonse Daudet
foreign.hook: A shepherd on the Luberon and the farm's daughter, stranded overnight by a flood, name the stars until she falls asleep.

foreign.title: Le Secret de maître Cornille
foreign.author: Alphonse Daudet
foreign.hook: The last windmill near Fontvieille keeps turning after the steam mills arrive, and the miller keeps a secret about why.

foreign.title: Maria Chapdelaine, chapitre 1
foreign.author: Louis Hémon
foreign.hook: Mass lets out at Péribonka on the edge of the Quebec forest, and the parish stands about in the snow trading news.

foreign.title: Хорь и Калиныч
foreign.author: Ivan Turgenev
foreign.hook: The first of the Sportsman's Sketches: a hunter stays with two peasant friends, one shrewd and one dreamy.

foreign.title: Метель
foreign.author: Alexander Pushkin
foreign.hook: A secret elopement, a snowstorm that scatters everyone, and a wedding that turns out not to be the one anybody planned.

foreign.title: Desde mi celda: Carta primera
foreign.author: Gustavo Adolfo Bécquer
foreign.hook: Bécquer writes to Madrid from a Cistercian monastery below the Moncayo, where he has gone for his health.

foreign.title: La Buenaventura
foreign.author: Pedro Antonio de Alarcón
foreign.hook: Alarcón's comic tale of a Granada fortune-teller, in three short parts.

foreign.title: El donador de almas, I
foreign.author: Amado Nervo
foreign.hook: The opening of Nervo's 1899 fantasy novella, in which a doctor is given a soul as a present.

foreign.title: Le avventure di Pinocchio, capitoli 1–3
foreign.author: Carlo Collodi
foreign.hook: A log that talks, two old carpenters who come to blows, and Geppetto starting on a puppet.

foreign.title: Missa do Galo
foreign.author: Machado de Assis
foreign.hook: A young man waits up on Christmas Eve to go to midnight mass, and talks late into the night with his host's wife.

foreign.title: 奥の細道 (一〜九)
foreign.titleEn: The Narrow Road to the Deep North, sections 1–9
foreign.author: Matsuo Bashō

foreign.title: 草枕 (一)
foreign.author: Natsume Sōseki
foreign.hook: A painter climbs a mountain path thinking about art and people. Some of the best-known opening lines in Japanese.

foreign.match: a chang yu shan hai jing
foreign.title: 阿长与山海经
foreign.titleEn: Ah Chang and the Book of Hills and Seas
foreign.author: Lu Xun
foreign.hook: Lu Xun remembers his childhood nurse, her superstitions, and the illustrated book she found for him.

foreign.title: 빈처
foreign.author: Hyun Jin-geon
foreign.hook: A struggling writer in 1920s Seoul and the wife who keeps believing in him.

foreign.title: Nang Bata Pa Kami, kabanata 1–3
foreign.author: Pura L. Medrano
foreign.hook: The opening chapters of a Tagalog book about childhood.

foreign.title: दो सखियाँ (१–२)
foreign.author: Premchand
foreign.hook: The first letters between two friends, in Premchand's story told entirely in letters.

foreign.title: Bröllopsmarschen
foreign.author: Selma Lagerlöf
foreign.hook: A short story by Selma Lagerlöf, from a selection of her tales read in Swedish.

foreign.title: Max Havelaar, eerste hoofdstuk
foreign.author: Multatuli
foreign.hook: Batavus Droogstoppel, coffee broker of the Lauriergracht, explains why he disapproves of poetry.

foreign.title: An Sagart agus an t-Easbog
foreign.author: Douglas Hyde (collector)
foreign.hook: A Connacht folk tale Douglas Hyde collected in the 1880s and 1890s. I haven't been able to check its content: vet before relying on it.

foreign.title: Bord, dæk dig
foreign.author: Brothers Grimm (Danish translation)
foreign.hook: Grimm, read in Danish: three brothers, three magic gifts and a dishonest innkeeper.

_about_foreign: 'foreign' entries are short pieces read in a place's own language, shown as a second card under tonight's story. langByCountry lists each country's languages in order of preference; where none has a recording, the page uses the nearest foreign entry by distance and says so.
